text:
Paul Cotter arrived in Vancouver from New Jersey as an energy forward, and the energy part is there: 81 hits in 24 games. The scoring has dried up. He's pointless in eight straight on 2.8 expected points, and the chances have thinned out too.

His four goals came early, on 16 shots, and that 25% shooting was never going to hold. The bigger concern is what happens when he's on the ice. Vancouver takes 38.7% of the shot attempts and 30% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, 12 points worse than the team without him. Evolving-Hockey had a similar read last season (his team created little with him on, bottom 8% of forwards), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his value, if it's there, isn't in creating offense.

He's quick (96th percentile in bursts over 20 mph) and was part of Vegas's 2023 Cup team, so the energy-line role is a real one. But on a Canucks team that has lost a lot of games this month, his line needs to stop bleeding chances before the points matter.
